en: Majjhima Nikāya 24,
The Discourse on the Chariot-Team (Rathavinītasutta):
Thus have I heard—
At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Place.
Then a number of bhikkhus from the native land, having completed the rains residence in their own country, approached the Blessed One;
having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, they sat down to one side. As they were sitting to one side...
The Blessed One said this to those bhikkhus:

“Bhikkhus, who among you in the native land is so esteemed by his fellow celibate companions from that native land as one who himself is few in desires and speaks to the bhikkhus on being few in desires,
and who himself is content and speaks to the bhikkhus on contentment?”
He is one who acts for the benefit of the bhikkhus; he himself is secluded and speaks to the bhikkhus on the subject of seclusion;
he himself is unassociated and speaks to the bhikkhus on the subject of non-association; he himself has aroused energy and speaks to the bhikkhus on the subject of the arousal of energy;
he himself is perfected in virtue and speaks to the bhikkhus on the subject of perfection in virtue; he himself...
He is himself accomplished in concentration and is one who speaks to the bhikkhus on the accomplishment of concentration;

he is himself accomplished in wisdom and is one who speaks to the bhikkhus on the accomplishment of wisdom; he is himself accomplished in liberation and is one who speaks to the bhikkhus on the accomplishment of liberation;
and he is himself accomplished in the knowledge and vision of liberation and is one who speaks to the bhikkhus on the accomplishment of the knowledge and vision of liberation.

“Venerable sir, is there a venerable one named Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta who, in his own native land, is thus esteemed by the monks who are his fellow brahmacārīs: ‘He is a doer for the monks, an instructor, an informant, a guide, an encourager, an inspirer, and an exhilarator’?
“Venerable sir, there is the venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta who, in his own native land, is thus esteemed by the monks who are his fellow brahmacārīs.”

‘He himself is of few desires and is one who speaks to the bhikkhus on fewness of desires; he himself is contented … [and so on] … he is an exhorter, an informer, an instructor, an encourager, an inspirer, and an exhilarator of his fellow celibates.
Now at that time the Venerable Sāriputta was sitting not far from the Blessed One.
Then it occurred to the Venerable Sāriputta:

“It is a gain for the venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta, a great gain for the venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta, that his wise fellow-celibates speak in the Teacher’s presence of his virtues one by one, and that the Teacher rejoices in them.
Perhaps we too might at some time meet with the venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta; perhaps there might be some conversation between us.”
Then the Blessed One, having stayed at Rājagaha for as long as he pleased, set out on a wandering tour toward Sāvatthī.
Traveling by stages on his tour, he arrived at Sāvatthī.
There the Blessed One dwelt at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
The Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta heard: “It is said that the Blessed One has arrived at Sāvatthī and is staying at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Then the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta, having put his lodging in order and taking his bowl and robe, set out on a wandering tour toward Sāvatthī.

Traveling by stages on his tour, he eventually reached Sāvatthī, Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery, and approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side.
As the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta was sitting to one side, the Blessed One instructed, exhorted, inspired, and gladdened him with a discourse on the Dhamma.

Then the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta, having been instructed, exhorted, inspired, and gladdened by the Blessed One with a discourse on the Dhamma, rejoiced and expressed his appreciation for the Blessed One’s words; then, rising from his seat, he approached the Blessed One.
Having paid homage and circumambulated him, he went to the Blind Men’s Grove for his midday rest.
Then a certain bhikkhu approached the Venerable Sāriputta; having approached, he said this to the Venerable Sāriputta:
“Friend Sāriputta, that bhikkhu named Puṇṇa, the son of Mantāṇī, whom you [have spoken of] frequently...”
While he was being praised, he was instructed, exhorted, inspired, and gladdened by the Blessed One with a discourse on the Dhamma.
Having rejoiced and delighted in the Blessed One’s words, he rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One,
and keeping him to his right, departed for the Blind Men’s Grove to dwell for the day.
Then the Venerable Sāriputta, in a great hurry, took his sitting mat and followed closely behind the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta, keeping his eyes fixed on the other’s head.
Then the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta, having plunged into the Blind Men’s Grove, sat down at the foot of a certain tree for his midday rest.
The Venerable Sāriputta also, having plunged into the Blind Men’s Grove, sat down at the foot of a certain tree for his midday rest.
Then, in the evening, the Venerable Sāriputta emerged from seclusion and approached the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta. Having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta.
When they had concluded their polite and courteous conversation, he sat down to one side. As he was sitting there, the Venerable Sāriputta said this to the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta:
"Friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One?"
“Yes, friend.
“But, friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the sake of purification of virtue?
“Certainly not, friend.”
“But, friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the sake of purification of mind?”—
“No indeed, friend.”— “Then, friend,
is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the sake of purification of view?”— “No indeed, friend.”
“No, friend.
“But then, friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the sake of purification by overcoming doubt?
“No, friend.”
“Friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the sake of purification by knowledge and vision of what is and is not the path?
“No, friend.
“But, friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the sake of purification by knowledge and vision of the way?”
“No, friend.
“Then, friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the sake of purification of knowledge and vision?
“No, friend.”
“When you were asked, ‘Friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the sake of purification of virtue? you replied, ‘No indeed, friend.
When you were asked, ‘But, friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the sake of purification of mind? you replied, ‘No indeed, friend.
When you were asked, ‘But, friend, is it for the sake of purification of view? … [and so on].”

For the sake of purification by overcoming doubt … for the sake of purification by knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path … for the sake of purification by knowledge and vision of the way … [and so on].
“Friend, when asked, ‘Is it for the sake of purification of knowledge and vision that the holy life is lived under the Blessed One? you replied, ‘No indeed, friend.
For what purpose, then, friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One?
“It is, friend, for the sake of final Nibbāna through non-clinging that the holy life is lived under the Blessed One.”
“Friend, is purification of virtue final Nibbāna through non-clinging?
“No, friend.
“But, friend, is purification of mind final Nibbāna through non-clinging?”
“No, friend.
“But what then, friend—is purification of view the final nibbāna through non-clinging?
“No, friend.”
“But, friend, is purification by overcoming doubt final Nibbāna without clinging?
“No, friend.
“Then, friend, is purification by knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path final Nibbāna without clinging?”
“No, friend.
“But, friend, is purification by knowledge and vision of the way the unbinding through non-clinging?
“No, friend.”
“Friend, is the purification of knowledge and vision itself the final Nibbāna through non-clinging?
“No indeed, friend.
“But, friend, is the final Nibbāna through non-clinging something other than these states?”
“No, friend.
“When asked, ‘Friend, is purification of virtue final Nibbāna without clinging? you replied, ‘No, friend.
When asked, ‘But friend, is purification of mind final Nibbāna without clinging? you replied, ‘No, friend.’”
‘Friend, is purification of view the final Nibbāna through non-clinging?

… [and so on] … purification by overcoming doubt … purification by knowledge and vision of what is and what is not the path … [and so on] … purification by knowledge and vision of the way … purification by knowledge and vision?
Regarding the purification by knowledge and vision of the way:
when asked, “Friend, is purification by knowledge and vision itself final Nibbāna through non-clinging? you replied, “No, friend.
When asked, “But friend, is final Nibbāna through non-clinging something other than these states? you replied, “No, friend.”
"But how, friend, is the meaning of this statement to be understood?
"Friend, if the Blessed One were to designate purification of virtue as final Nibbāna without clinging, he would be designating final Nibbāna without clinging for one who still possesses clinging.
If the Blessed One were to designate purification of mind as final Nibbāna without clinging, he would be designating final Nibbāna without clinging for one who still possesses clinging."
"Friend, if the Blessed One were to designate purification of view as final Nibbāna without clinging, he would be designating final Nibbāna without clinging for one who still possesses clinging.

If, friend, the Blessed One were to designate purification by overcoming doubt as final Nibbāna without clinging, he would be designating final Nibbāna without clinging for one who still possesses clinging.

If, friend, the Blessed One were to designate purification by knowledge and vision of what is and is not the path as final Nibbāna without clinging, he would be designating final Nibbāna without clinging for one who still possesses clinging."

Friend, if the Blessed One were to designate purification by knowledge and vision as final Nibbāna without clinging, he would be designating what is still accompanied by clinging as final Nibbāna without clinging.

If the Blessed One were to designate purification by knowledge and vision as final Nibbāna without clinging, he would be designating what is still accompanied by clinging as final Nibbāna without clinging.
For if, friend, final Nibbāna without clinging were to exist apart from these states, then an ordinary person would attain final Nibbāna.
For an ordinary person, friend, is apart from these qualities.
Therefore, friend, I shall give you a simile;
for by means of a simile some wise people understand the meaning of what is said.
"Suppose, friends, King Pasenadi of Kosala, while residing in Sāvatthī, were to have some urgent business arise in Sāketa.
Between Sāvatthī and Sāketa, seven relay chariots would be stationed for him.
Then, friends, King Pasenadi of Kosala, having departed from Sāvatthī, [would emerge] from the gate of his inner palace first..."

He would mount one chariot-horseman; having reached the second chariot-horseman by means of the first chariot-horseman, he would leave the first chariot-horseman and mount the second chariot-horseman.
Having reached the third chariot-horseman by means of the second chariot-horseman, he would leave the second chariot-horseman and mount the third chariot-horseman.
By means of the third chariot-station, one would reach the fourth chariot-station; one would leave the third chariot-station and mount the fourth chariot-station.
By means of the fourth chariot-station, one would reach the fifth chariot-station; one would leave the fourth chariot-station and mount the fifth chariot-station.
By means of the fifth chariot-station, one would reach the sixth chariot-station; one would leave the fifth chariot-station and mount the sixth chariot-station.
From the sixth chariot-station he would reach the seventh chariot-station; he would leave the sixth chariot-station and mount the seventh chariot-station.
From the seventh chariot-station he would arrive at Sāketa, at the gate of the inner palace.
When he had reached the gate of the inner palace, his friends, companions, kinsmen, and blood relations would ask him thus:
“‘Great King, did you arrive at the gate of the inner palace in Sāketa from Sāvatthī by means of this chariot-horse team?
How, friend, would King Pasenadi of Kosala answer correctly if he were to answer rightly?
“Answering in this way, friend, King Pasenadi of Kosala would answer correctly: ‘I arrived at the gate of the inner palace in Sāketa from Sāvatthī by means of this chariot-horse team.’”
"While I was residing here in Sāvatthī, a certain urgent matter arose for me in Sāketa.
For that purpose, they provided seven chariot teams for me between Sāvatthī and Sāketa.
Then, having departed from Sāvatthī, I mounted the first chariot team at the gate of the inner palace."
With the first chariot team I reached the second chariot team; I left the first chariot team and mounted the second.
With the second chariot team I reached the third chariot team; I left the second chariot team and mounted the third.
With the third chariot team I reached the fourth chariot team; I left the third chariot team and mounted the fourth.
By means of the fourth chariot-yoke, I reached the fifth chariot-yoke; I left behind the fourth chariot-yoke and mounted the fifth chariot-yoke.
By means of the fifth chariot-yoke, I reached the sixth chariot-yoke; I left behind the fifth chariot-yoke and mounted the sixth chariot-yoke.
By means of the sixth chariot-yoke, I reached the seventh chariot-yoke; I left behind the sixth chariot-yoke and mounted the seventh chariot-yoke.
"Having reached Sāketa on the seventh chariot journey, he has arrived at the gate of the inner palace.
"Friend, if King Pasenadi of Kosala were to answer thus, he would be answering correctly.
"In the same way, friend, purification of virtue is for the sake of purification of mind; purification of mind is for the sake of..."

Purification of view is for the sake of purification by overcoming doubt; purification by overcoming doubt is for the sake of purification by knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path;
purification by knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path is for the sake of purification by knowledge and vision of the way;
purification by knowledge and vision of the way is for the sake of purification by knowledge and vision.
“Purification of knowledge and vision is for the sake of final Nibbāna without clinging.
Indeed, friend, the holy life is lived under the Blessed One for the sake of final Nibbāna without clinging.
When this was said, the Venerable Sāriputta said this to the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta:
“What is the venerable one’s name, and how do his fellow celibates know him?
“My name is Puṇṇa, friend,
and my fellow celibates know me as Mantāṇiputta.”
“It is wonderful, friend! It is marvelous, friend!
Just as a learned disciple who rightly understands the Teacher’s instruction would do, so too has the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta answered these profound questions point by point.
It is a gain for his fellow celibates, it is a great boon for his fellow celibates!”
Those who obtain the opportunity to see the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta and to attend upon him have gained a great benefit;

they have gained a great boon. Even if fellow celibates were to carry the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta on their heads like a ceremonial cloth-wrapped bundle while seeking to see him and attend upon him, even for them it would be a gain, it would be well-gained; and for us as well...
“It is a gain for us too, a great fortune that we have the opportunity to see the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta and to attend upon him.
When this was said, the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta said this to the Venerable Sāriputta:
“What is the Venerable One’s name, and how do his fellow practitioners know him?
“My name is Upatissa, friend,
and my fellow practitioners know me as Sāriputta.”
“Indeed, sir, while consulting with a disciple who is as if the Teacher himself,
we did not realize it was the Venerable Sāriputta.
For had we known it was the Venerable Sāriputta, we would not have spoken even this much.”
"It is wonderful, friend! It is marvelous, friend!
Just as a learned disciple who rightly understands the Teacher’s instruction would do, so has the Venerable Sāriputta asked these profound questions, one by one.
It is a gain for our fellow practitioners, it is a great boon for our fellow practitioners!"
Those who obtain the opportunity to see the Venerable Sāriputta obtain the opportunity to attend upon him.

Even if fellow celibates were to carry the Venerable Sāriputta on their heads like a cloth-wrapped turban while obtaining the opportunity to see him and obtain the opportunity to attend upon him, it would be a gain for them, it would be well-acquired by them; it is also a gain for us.
“It has been gained by us as well, that we have obtained the venerable Sāriputta for the purpose of seeing him and obtaining him for the purpose of attending upon him.
And so these two great nāgas both rejoiced in each other’s well-spoken words.
The Rathavinīta Sutta is finished; it is the fourth.
